claims.claim_ar: استعمال حرف النداء «يا» لالتفات المخاطبين (نداء المؤمنين وإلقاء الانتباه)
claims.claim_en: Use of the vocative particle «يا» to turn attention to the addressees (calling the believers; vocative attention/shift).
claims.rhetorical_effect: directs attention to the audience, creates immediacy and moral pressure

claims.claim_ar: مقابلة/تضاد بين المؤمنين والكافرين لإبراز التباين والتهديد بخسارة المؤمنين إن التحقوا بالكافرين
claims.claim_en: Antithesis (muqabalah) between the believers and the disbelievers to highlight contrast and the warning that believers who follow the disbelievers will suffer loss.
claims.rhetorical_effect: sharpens moral polarity; strengthens the warning by opposing two groups

claims.claim_ar: استعمال حرف الفاء الاستئنافي (الفاء في «فَتَنْقَلِبُوا») لربط النتيجة بالشرط وإبرازهما: فاء ربط واستئناف تؤكد الجزاء
claims.claim_en: Use of the consecutive/resumptive particle «fa» (as in «fa-tanqalibū») to link the consequence to the condition and to foreground the resulting punishment — a connective that emphasizes the outcome.
claims.rhetorical_effect: foregrounds the consequence; creates causal immediacy and emphasis

claims.source_quote_ar: واعلم أنّ هذه الآية وردت منظومة من غير قصد
claims.claim_ar: ملاحظة بلاغية/عروضية: النص يرد منظوماً على بحر (ذكر المصدر أنّ الآية ظهرت منظومة، بيت كامل من مجزوء الرّمل)، أي وجود بعد إيقاعي/نظمي في صياغة الآية
claims.claim_en: Rhetorical/prosodic observation: the verse appears in a metrically patterned (organized) line — the source notes it appears as a full hemistich on the meter 'majzūʾ al-raml', indicating an incidental rhythmic/metrical shaping.
claims.needs_review_reason: the quoted source passage speaks generally about 'هذه الآية' being metrically organized; confirm that the source was referring specifically to this verse (S3:149) and not to another verse in the commentary.
claims.rhetorical_effect: adds perceptible rhythmic cadence that can increase memorability and emphasis

warnings: Provided source chunks are grammatical/iʿrāb notes (Darwish - I'rab); they are not the classical balagha authors named in the task (al-Jurjani, al-Sakkaki, al-Baqillani, al-Suyuti, tafsir-balagha). Claims are therefore drawn from these iʿrāb chunks and may not reflect full classical rhetorical commentary.

Some quoted passages (e.g., the prosody note) are generic statements using the phrase «هذه الآية» in the source; please verify that the source passage indeed refers to Sūrah 3:149 specifically before using that claim as authoritative for this ayah.

I limited claims to devices listed in the instructions. Other plausible rhetorical readings (e.g., conditional warning force of «إن»; the repetition of «الذين» for emphasis) could be added but lacked direct, explicit support in the provided chunks and so were not asserted with high confidence.
